key_insight: A new two-way QKD protocol uses a Bell-state qubit plus a scrambling operator, with all sifting and eavesdropper checks deferred to the end and performed only by Bob.
engineering_relevance: The design improves protocol robustness by removing public control-mode announcements and turning normally discarded rounds into useful security checks, which may simplify secure quantum link operation.
method: Use one qubit from a maximally entangled Bell state as the quantum channel.
Apply a scrambling operator to add security without directly encoding key information on the traveling qubit.
Postpone sifting and eavesdropper detection until after quantum transmission, with Bob handling the checks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical security analysis of a broad class of ancilla-based attacks and shows they are detectable in their most general form.
watch_item: The protocol’s practical value depends on implementing delayed, Bob-only post-processing and the scrambling operation without introducing new noise or synchronization overhead.
